comparisons.peer_topic: Securities Financing Agreements Purpose and Accounting
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation utilizes securities financing agreements, referred to as matched-book transactions, to accommodate customers, cover short positions, and finance inventory. Certain of these agreements are accounted for under the fair value option, with further details provided in Note 21.
comparisons.comparison: While Citi's ACL on other assets includes a specific historical transfer of $30 million for 'securities borrowed and purchased under agreements to resell' activities, Bank of America discloses that it utilizes securities financing agreements which 'include securities borrowed or purchased under agreements to resell' as part of its matched-book transactions. Both companies identify this specific financing activity as a source of assets or collateral requiring accounting treatment, though Citi quantifies the specific legacy ACL transfer amount while BAC describes the broader business purpose and accounting election.
